clue.text: Horrified to see a horrible gash on shirt

indicators.note: something horrible is a mess, so the letters of gash are jumbled

parts.note: a T-shirt or tee gives the letter T

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled at an ugly cut showing on a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' is the anagram signal on the cut; the shirt supplies a tee, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone struck with shock and dismay.

clue.text: Fish found on north-east French river

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
taken as written
NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: A fish is caught on a river in north-eastern France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garonne is a major river of south-west France flowing to Bordeaux.

clue.text: Tore "Iliad" to shreds in article

indicators.note: tearing something to shreds breaks it into bits, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ripped up a copy of Homer's epic, as reported in an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shreds' rearranges the letters of TORE ILIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading article in a newspaper is called an editorial.

clue.text: Forbid cap being put on bird

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: to forbid is to ban
a tam is a Scottish woollen cap (tam-o'-shanter)

explanation.surface: A ban is placed on making a bird wear a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of domestic fowl.

clue.text: A village setting for Shakespeare's play

definitions.meaning: the tragedy of the Prince of Denmark

explanation.surface: A small village serves as the backdrop for a Shakespeare production.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny village without a church is one sense; the Danish prince's tragedy is the other.

clue.text: Reduce aid to the impotent

parts.note: to aid is to help
to reduce something is to make it less

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut back assistance to the powerless.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Reduce aid' as 'help less', with the pieces in the reverse order of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Being powerless to act is the shared sense of the two words.

clue.text: Suitable to have Sabbath fox-hunt fixtures?

parts.note: meet is an old word for fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: Asking whether Sunday is a fitting day to hold hunting events.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunt's meet is the gathering where riders and hounds assemble before setting off.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunt meetings are called meets, scheduled gatherings of riders and hounds.

clue.text: Praised former sound editor

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a bell tolls when it sounds

explanation.surface: A past sound editor received praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud highly, so the past form means lauded.

clue.text: Person in charge of a newspaper

definitions.meaning: someone with responsibility for another, such as a ward

explanation.surface: Someone who runs a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodian of a child is one sense; a British daily paper's title is the other.

clue.text: Customers throwing money around long island

indicators.note: the money word goes around the island abbreviation

parts.note: cents are small coins, money

explanation.surface: Shoppers splashing cash around Long Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing' is surface colour only; 'around' is the container signal, with the island abbreviation sitting just after the first letter of the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Customers of a business or professional are its patrons or buyers.

clue.text: Concerning a boxing match

definitions.meaning: a bout is a single contest in the ring

explanation.surface: Something to do with a fight in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means regarding; split as A BOUT it is one contest.

clue.text: Object to the French being secretive while lacking purpose

parts.note: an object or goal is an aim
les is the French plural form of 'the'
sly means furtive or secretive

explanation.surface: Objecting to the French being secretive while having no clear goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Without direction or goal, the adverb describes drifting activity.

clue.text: Is a savings account the answer?

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a savings account is the solution.
explanation.walkthrough: ISA is a UK tax-free savings account (Individual Savings Account); the clue's first two words simply spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: An Individual Savings Account is a British tax-free deposit scheme.

clue.text: Fits of temper after worker gets booze in back street

indicators.note: the worker and booze go inside the street abbreviation
back means the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker
rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: Outbursts after a labourer gets drink in a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the street abbreviation round, and 'in' puts the worker and drink between its two letters; 'after' and 'gets' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish outbursts of rage are what both expressions denote.

clue.text: Lots of goals!

parts.note: a lot of goals is one reading; lots as in many twenties is the other hidden sense

explanation.definitionFit: Large numbers of points or goals in matches, and many twenties, both fit the plural.

clue.text: Drinks for the old sahib

parts.note: small measures of whisky taken by British colonials in Raj-era India

explanation.definitionFit: In British India a small peg of spirits, chota meaning small in Hindi, was a common tot.

clue.text: Sorry, writer and I need to take shelter!

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a tent is a temporary shelter

explanation.surface: An apology from a writer who has to take cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone remorseful for wrongdoing is contrite.

clue.text: Everyone, or just some wallachians

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the word are used, a run within it

explanation.surface: Is it everybody, or only certain people from Wallachia?
explanation.walkthrough: Wallachians are people of Wallachia, a region of Romania.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole group, every person, is meant by both.

clue.text: Playing lyres and looking for Hermia's lover

indicators.note: playing music on lyres is the surface; here it says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strumming lyres while searching for the man Hermia loves.
explanation.walkthrough: In A Midsummer Night's Dream, Hermia loves Lysander. 'Playing' rearranges LYRES AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comedy pairs Hermia with this young Athenian.

clue.text: A quiet route to the remains

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A peaceful path to a burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the residue left after burning, especially cremated human residue.

clue.text: Concerning a friend, in fact

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Talking about a friend, in truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean actually or truly.

clue.text: Primate seen in a pentecostal church

indicators.note: the letters can be seen running across the words that follow

explanation.surface: A monkey spotted inside a Pentecostal church.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas and chimpanzees are examples of this kind of primate.

clue.text: People getting on, we hear, in southern Scotland

indicators.note: we hear signals that what is said aloud matters, not the spelling

parts.note: passengers getting on a ship or plane are boarders

explanation.surface: Passengers embarking somewhere in the south of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Borders is the region of southern Scotland next to England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish Borders is the region running along the English frontier.

clue.text: Office amenity created after space is provided

parts.note: post means after, as in post-war
room means space

explanation.surface: A workplace facility built once space has been found.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail sorting area is a facility in many workplaces.

clue.text: Decree that ordnance should be Scots' own

parts.note: ORD is an abbreviation for ordnance
ain is the Scots word for own

explanation.surface: An order that military weapons belong to the Scottish people.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to order or appoint by authority.

clue.text: Illness caught by boy in springtime

indicators.note: the boy is held inside the springtime month

parts.note: May is a month of spring
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy picks up a sickness in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease or ailment is what both words name.

clue.text: A short cut, perhaps, taken to avert semi-circular route

indicators.note: a circular route goes round, so the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: A quicker way taken to avoid going halfway around a loop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circular route' rearranges AVERT and SEMI; 'perhaps' marks a short cut as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A short cut is one example of something that cuts down the hours spent.

clue.text: Report of a woman producing wheat

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the spoken form counts

parts.note: Emma is a woman's name

explanation.surface: News of a woman growing a crop.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech EMMA and EMMER sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmer is an ancient variety of grain cultivated since prehistoric times.

clue.text: Cycle for exercise and pulse

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
dal is a dish of lentils, a pulse

explanation.surface: Riding a bike for fitness and heart rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To cycle is to ride a bike by pushing its foot-levers round.

clue.text: Could be a drum playing before the triangle

indicators.note: playing a drum is the surface; here the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An orchestral player could be on drum before switching to the triangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges BE A DRUM. The Bermuda Triangle is the area of the Atlantic famed for vanishing ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bermuda Triangle is a stretch of the western Atlantic linked with disappearances.

clue.text: Damaged green lid got left behind

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken green lid was abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawdling or staying on after others go means trailing in the rear.

clue.text: Arrest warped voyeur

indicators.note: warped means bent out of shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Detain a twisted peeping Tom.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyeur is someone who gazes, a person who looks fixedly.
